verdict_reason: All 17 findings of this part are fixed in the code at HEAD (F16-3 completing only at fdf193a's tree kill), and the residual issues found are minor/note-level, none blocking.

findings.claim: c3 router explain, previously a purely local computation, now builds the panel's member election with skip_preflight=false and reads budget multipliers in network mode, so a display command can spawn credential/auth probes for every active roster entry and has no deadline bounding it.
findings.trigger: A roster with claude-engine or codex entries whose credentials need probing (no cached health) when the operator runs c3 router explain.

evidence.observation: seat_marks calls Ctx::for_consult, pctx.panel_members("", "", purpose, false, false, 0, false) (skip_preflight=false) and member_inputs(..., !pctx.no_network).
panel_members with skip_preflight=false runs preflight per entry, which for claude/http/other engines calls engine_credential probes.

findings.verification: Run c3 router explain on a roster with one unauthenticated claude entry while listing spawned processes and timing the command.
findings.remedy: Pass skip_preflight=true (or cache-only budget mode) in explain's election, or document and deadline-bound the probes; the marks only need relative eligibility.

findings.claim: tier_missed_warning drops the warning entirely when any eligible weighty candidate's lab holds no seat, including the case where required pins already fill all k seats so no tier seat could be drawn: an eligible weighty entry is seated, no required entry is weighty, and the plan stays silent, contrary to the stated invariant.
findings.trigger: A weighty purpose, panel size k equal to the number of required pins (labs A and B), and a panel:weighty entry of a third lab C: invoke_lab_draw skips the tier seat because seats.len() >= k, and seated_at(lab C) is None so the `?` returns no warning.

evidence.observation: `let by = seated_at(&c.lab)?;` inside the loop over tier candidates returns None from the whole function when the lab is unseated.
The tier seat is only drawn when seats.len() < k, so pins filling the panel skip it without a tier rule ever appearing (which would have suppressed the warning at plan.rs:1216 anyway).

findings.verification: Unit-test select_panel_routing with two required pins filling size 2 and a weighty third-lab entry on a weighty purpose; assert a warning or its documented absence.
findings.remedy: When a tier candidate's lab is unseated, still warn (naming no 'held by' lab, e.g. 'no room beside the required seats') instead of returning None.

findings.claim: Two SessionStart hooks starting concurrently in the SAME repository both pass gate_due before either writes, so both call gh and both print: 'at most once a day per repository' does not hold for simultaneous starts (the fix removed only the cross-repository read-modify-write).
findings.trigger: Two sessions start in one repository within the window between gate_due's read and gate_record's rename.

evidence.observation: gate_due reads the per-repo file, then gate_record writes it; no create-exclusive or lock guards the same-key window.
The concurrency test covers two different repositories only.

findings.verification: Start two c3 hook processes together in one fresh repo with a logging fake gh and count gh invocations.
findings.remedy: Accept and document the same-repo window, or create the gate file exclusively (create_new) and let the loser skip.

findings.claim: recorded_draw silently drops malformed rows (filter_map), so a partially valid ext.c3.draw makes the replay weigh precise values for some candidates and rounded values for others without saying so; only a fully absent block produces the rounded note.
findings.trigger: A ledger record whose ext.c3.draw has a row missing position/score or with mult <= 0 or non-finite.

evidence.observation: Rows are filter_map'd; per-candidate fallback to e.score * recorded_mult(e) is silent.

findings.verification: Feed replay_one a record with one valid and one malformed draw row and inspect whether any note or failure is produced.
findings.remedy: Treat a draw block with any invalid row as absent (note the rounding) or fail the replay with a message.

findings.claim: Host-equal recognition narrows coverage: a remote at https://www.github.com/... (previously matched by the substring test, and a real GitHub alias) is now silent, as are ssh-alias remotes (gh:owner/repo via ~/.ssh/config) - the alias case was silent before too.
findings.trigger: A repository whose only remote URL host is www.github.com (or an ssh alias whose configured hostname is github.com) with a red default-branch run.

evidence.observation: url_host returns the literal host and remotes_name_github compares == "github.com"; no www or alias handling.

evidence.reference: old code (patch hunk at ci_check.rs remotes_name_github)
evidence.observation: The previous contains("github.com/") matched www.github.com URLs.

findings.verification: Point a scratch repo's origin at https://www.github.com/example/c3.git with a fake gh and confirm no CI line and zero gh calls.
findings.remedy: Also accept www.github.com (a one-line host check), or document the exact-host rule.

findings.claim: A gate temp file whose process dies between write and rename is never cleaned: its name (json.<pid>.<nanos>.tmp) fails is_gate_file_name, and the 30-day prune only touches gate-named files.
findings.trigger: c3 hook is killed in the milliseconds between fs::write of the temp file and the rename.

evidence.observation: Tmp is removed only when rename fails; the prune loop skips non-gate names.

findings.verification: Kill a hook mid gate_record in a fixture and list the c3 directory afterwards.
findings.remedy: Also remove stale ci-check-*.tmp files older than GATE_KEEP_DAYS during the prune.

- **F16-3 fixed** — `ci_check.rs:297` / `:418` run the whole check inside `bounded::within` (10 s / 3 s); `crates/c3/src/bounded.rs:45` `stop()` now kills child + descendants via `crates/c3/src/engines/subprocess.rs:1262` `kill_tree_by_pid`. Caveat: complete only at fdf193a; 748ba3a alone killed no descendants (its Windows CI failed, as the brief admits).
- **F16-4 / F17-7 fixed** — `crates/c3/src/setup/branches.rs:319` `remote_default_branch` (origin/HEAD without a local twin), used by `ci_check.rs:254` `ci_branch`; time-parsed ordering `ci_check.rs:170-177`; limit 20 `:49`.

- **F16-9 fixed** — per-repo gate file `ci_check.rs:341`, `repo_key` `:322`, `gate_due` `:351`, `gate_record` `:374` (temp+rename, legacy shared file removed, 30-day prune).
- **F16-6 / F17-2 fixed** — `crates/c3/src/cli/router.rs:187-229` `seat_marks` uses `pctx.panel_members` (`:204`), `crates/c3/src/panel/run.rs:214` `member_inputs`, `crates/c3/src/panel/plan.rs:1263` `lab_seat_marks`, `crates/c3/src/panel/routing.rs:818` `lab_stands`; replay weighs `ext.c3.draw` (`crates/c3/src/router/replay.rs:240`, `:106`) and notes rounded replays (`:365`).
- **F16-7 / F17-4 fixed** — `plan.rs:26` table (+`minimax`/`meta-llama`/`llama`), `:49` aliases whole-id only, `:58` `prefix_at_boundary`, `:136` case-folded `entry_lab`, `:151` `member_lab`; host/prefix agreement unit-tested.

- **F17-6 fixed** — `crates/c3/src/setup/rules.rs:96-115` `with_branches_section` appends only (no existing byte changes); docs now state the title-line-alone rule (`rules.rs:66`); proven by `crates/c3-cli/tests/delegation_rule.rs:247`.

## Q2 — legitimate refusals
The branch filter drops only what git ref names cannot contain (control/space/format), so no valid ref loses the line; a `c3.defaultBranch` value with a space drops it silently (safe direction). Remote-host equality loses `https://www.github.com/...` remotes (matched by the old substring test) and ssh-alias remotes (`gh:owner/repo` via ~/.ssh/config — silent before too): finding #5. Remote-only defaults now work (tested). The boundary rule can split one maker into two labs (`seed` vs `seedream`, both ByteDance) so such siblings may share a panel; no seat a roster needs is kept out.

## Q3 — leftovers
Descendants are killed at HEAD (tree enumerated before `taskkill /T`, identity-checked loop `subprocess.rs:1273-1283`); a grandchild spawned after enumeration can still escape — inherent. Temp gate files are removed on rename failure but survive a crash mid-write and are never pruned (`ci_check.rs:399` name filter) — finding #6. Stale gate files are pruned only when some repository records. The worker thread is abandoned past the deadline (documented, `bounded.rs:146`); it ends once its children die.

## Q4 — unintended callers
`"ci"` in `c3 finish --json` changed from string to object (`crates/c3/src/cli/finish.rs:118`) — breaking for old consumers, documented. The branch line shares `bounded` unchanged and gains the tree kill. Panels: same-maker families split by boundary labs (above). `router explain` now runs the panel's election with preflight and network budget reads and no deadline (`cli/router.rs:195-205`) — finding #1.

## Q5 — Windows vs Unix
The scripts agree for ASCII lines (ps1 `Get-CutText` equals `Substring` for ASCII; awk bytes == chars). CHANGELOG sentences of this part now match the code, including the withdrawn byte-identical claim and the append-only delegation wording; "at most once a day per repository" still has the same-repo concurrent-start exception (finding #3).

## Q6 — untested
Same-repo concurrent gate race; `www.github.com` remotes; end-to-end `router explain` with real preflight (only `lab_seat_marks` is unit-tested; the .ps1 surrogate tests run on Windows only); the pins-fill-panel tier-miss edge (finding #2); malformed `ext.c3.draw` rows (finding #4); real `gh` `event` value variants.

## Requested checks
- **RC1** — In a scratch repo, configure `--require` entries of two labs, panel size 2, plus a `panel: weighty` entry of a third lab, on a weighty purpose; run `c3 consult --panel --dry-run` (workspace-write). Observation: no `upper tier missed` warning appears although no weighty entry is seated (finding #2). Budget: ~10 min.
- **RC2** — Start two `c3 hook` processes simultaneously in one fresh repo with a logging fake `gh` on PATH (read-only fixture). Observation: two gh invocations the same day for one repository (finding #3). Budget: ~10 min.
- **RC3** — Run `c3 router explain` on a roster with one unauthenticated claude-engine entry; list spawned processes and elapsed time. Observation: credential probes spawned by a display command, unbounded duration (finding #1). Budget: ~10 min.
- **RC4** — Scratch repo whose origin is `https://www.github.com/example/c3.git`, fake `gh` logging calls; run `c3 hook`. Observation: zero gh calls, no CI line (finding #5). Budget: ~5 min.
